name: res-switch
desc: Free, open-source display mode switcher for Windows — save resolution, refresh and layout profiles, hotkey them. 100 MB portable, MIT.
features: ✅ **Full display profiles** — resolution, refresh rate, orientation and primary-display flag saved together
✅ **Tray and hotkey switching** — Ctrl+Alt+1 through 4 apply profiles in about a second
✅ **Per-game auto-apply** — bind a profile to a game exe and it engages when that process starts
✅ **Safe revert countdown** — a 15-second keep-or-revert dialog protects against black-screen modes
✅ **Refresh-rate fixer** — jumps a 60 Hz monitor back to its 144 Hz setting after driver updates
✅ **Multi-monitor sets** — laptop-only, docked and TV sets stored with per-monitor modes
✅ **100 MB self-contained exe** — runtime bundled, portable, offline, MIT with SHA-256 releases
compare: | Full profiles with refresh | **Yes** | Yes | Yes | No |
| Safe revert countdown | **Yes** | No | Yes | No |
| Portable, no install | **Yes, 100 MB** | Tray app | Installer | With OS |
faqQ: how to quickly change screen resolution and refresh rate on Windows?
faqA: Windows display settings need a dialog crawl every time, which adds up when switching between a competitive game and desktop work. res-switch stores complete profiles and applies them from a hotkey or automatically when a game launches, with a revert countdown if the mode is wrong. It is a 100 MB portable exe, MIT, offline.
s1: Dark profile cards (#121418, teal #2DD4BF): Gaming 2560x1440 at 144 Hz, Desktop 4K at 60 Hz, Movie 1080p; hotkey badges, active card glowing.
s2: Profile editor: resolution dropdown, refresh selector, orientation and primary toggles, revert timeout slider at 15 s.
s3: Game bindings: exe list with attached profiles, countdown dialog preview over a black screenshot, tray behavior options.
